goals.title: Establish security governance and risk management
goals.objective: A written program charter, named security roles, core policies, and a living risk register are approved and in active use across the business.
goals.why: It reduces the risk of unmanaged, unaccountable security decisions by making ownership, priorities, and acceptable risk explicit for leadership.
kpis: Percent of core policies (acceptable use, access, data, incident response) approved and published (target 100%)
Percent of defined security roles with a named, accountable owner (target 100%)
Percent of identified risks in the register with an owner and treatment decision (target 90%+)
Frequency of leadership risk review (target at least quarterly)
milestones: Draft and approve a one-page security program charter signed by leadership
Assign security roles and responsibilities (owner, decision-maker, day-to-day contact)
Write and publish the core policy set in plain English
Stand up a risk register and complete an initial risk assessment
Assign an owner and treatment decision (accept, mitigate, transfer, avoid) to each top risk
Schedule a recurring quarterly leadership risk review

goals.title: Build and maintain an authoritative asset inventory
goals.objective: A single authoritative inventory of hardware, software, and data assets exists, is actively maintained, and flags unauthorized assets for review.
goals.why: It reduces the risk of blind spots by ensuring you can only protect, patch, and monitor what you know you have.
kpis: Percent of known hardware assets recorded in the authoritative inventory (target 95%+)
Percent of installed software recorded and marked authorized or unauthorized (target 95%+)
Number of unauthorized assets detected and resolved per month (target trending down)
Maximum age of the inventory since last reconciliation (target under 30 days)
milestones: Select a single system of record for the asset inventory
Discover and record all hardware assets, including remote and mobile devices
Inventory installed software and label each entry authorized or unauthorized
Catalog data assets and where they are stored (on-premises, cloud, SaaS)
Define a process to review and remove or approve unauthorized assets
Set a recurring monthly reconciliation and assign an inventory owner

goals.title: Implement identity and access management controls
goals.objective: MFA, least-privilege access, a joiner-mover-leaver process, and privileged-account controls are enforced across critical systems.
goals.why: It reduces the risk of account takeover and insider misuse, the most common paths attackers use to reach business data.
kpis: Percent of accounts protected by MFA (target 100% of privileged, 95%+ overall)
Mean time to disable a departed employee's access (target under 24 hours)
Percent of privileged accounts reviewed and justified per quarter (target 100%)
Number of active accounts with no recent login flagged for review (target trending to zero)
milestones: Enable MFA on email, remote access, and administrative accounts first
Inventory accounts and separate standard from privileged access
Define and document a joiner-mover-leaver access process
Apply least-privilege by removing access that is not needed for a role
Establish dedicated, monitored privileged accounts separate from daily-use accounts
Schedule a recurring quarterly access review of privileged and dormant accounts

goals.title: Classify and protect sensitive data
goals.objective: Sensitive data is identified, classified by a simple tiered scheme, encrypted at rest and in transit, and governed by handling rules.
goals.why: It reduces the risk and cost of a breach by ensuring the most sensitive data is the most tightly controlled and encrypted.
kpis: Percent of identified sensitive data stores that carry a classification label (target 95%+)
Percent of sensitive data encrypted at rest and in transit (target 100%)
Percent of sensitive data stores with documented access and retention rules (target 90%+)
Number of sensitive data locations discovered outside approved systems (target trending to zero)
milestones: Define a simple data classification scheme (for example public, internal, confidential)
Discover and map where sensitive data lives across systems and SaaS
Apply classification labels to identified data stores
Enable encryption at rest and in transit for confidential data
Write plain-English handling and retention rules for each classification tier
Restrict access to confidential data to only the roles that need it

goals.title: Deploy hardened secure configuration baselines
goals.objective: Documented hardened baselines exist for operating systems, key software, and cloud services, and systems are measured against them.
goals.why: It reduces the risk of easy compromise by closing insecure default settings before attackers can exploit them.
kpis: Percent of system types with a documented hardened baseline (target 100% of critical types)
Percent of in-scope systems measured against their baseline (target 90%+)
Percent of measured systems compliant with their baseline (target 90%+)
Mean time to remediate a baseline drift finding (target under 30 days)
milestones: Adopt recognized hardening guidance (for example CIS Benchmarks) as a starting point
Document baselines for common operating systems and key business software
Define secure configuration standards for cloud and SaaS admin settings
Apply baselines to a pilot set of systems and confirm functionality
Measure in-scope systems against baselines and log any drift
Set a recurring cadence to review baselines and remediate drift

goals.title: Stand up continuous vulnerability scanning and risk-based patching
goals.objective: You will scan all assets on a regular schedule and remediate findings against documented, severity-based SLAs.
goals.why: Reduces the window attackers have to exploit known, fixable weaknesses before you close them.
kpis: Mean time to remediate critical vulnerabilities (target under 15 days)
Percent of in-scope assets scanned in the last 30 days (target 95%+)
Percent of vulnerabilities remediated within their severity SLA (target 90%+)
milestones: Deploy an authenticated vulnerability scanner across servers, endpoints, and external-facing systems
Define severity tiers and remediation SLAs (for example critical 15 days, high 30 days, medium 90 days)
Schedule recurring scans and route findings to owners through a ticketing workflow
Enable automated patch deployment for operating systems and common third-party software
Publish a monthly remediation report tracking SLA compliance and aging findings

goals.title: Harden email, web, and DNS against malware and phishing
goals.objective: You will filter malicious email and web traffic, enforce DNS filtering, and publish email authentication records for all owned domains.
goals.why: Reduces the risk that phishing, malicious attachments, and drive-by sites deliver malware or steal credentials.
kpis: Percent of inbound email passing DMARC enforcement (target 100 percent of owned domains at p=reject)
Percent of workstations enforcing DNS filtering (target 98 percent+)
Percent of email gateway malware and phishing detections quarantined before delivery (target 99 percent+)
milestones: Publish SPF, DKIM, and DMARC records for every owned domain and move DMARC to p=quarantine then p=reject
Enable inbound email filtering with attachment sandboxing and link rewriting
Roll out DNS filtering to block known malicious and newly registered domains
Deploy anti-malware with signature and behavioral detection on mail and web gateways
Configure alerting and a review cadence for blocked and quarantined items

goals.title: Deploy EDR and host hardening across all endpoints
goals.objective: You will have endpoint detection and response with anti-malware installed and reporting healthy on every managed device, plus a baseline hardening standard.
goals.why: Reduces the risk that a compromised device goes undetected and gives responders the visibility to contain threats quickly.
kpis: Percent of endpoints with EDR reporting healthy (target 98 percent+)
Percent of endpoints meeting the hardening baseline (target 95 percent+)
Mean time to isolate a flagged endpoint (target under 1 hour)
milestones: Select and deploy an EDR agent with anti-malware to all workstations and servers
Reconcile EDR coverage against the asset inventory and close gaps
Define a host hardening baseline (disable unused services, enforce disk encryption, restrict local admin)
Enable automated or one-click endpoint isolation for confirmed threats
Route EDR alerts to a monitored queue with defined triage steps
Report weekly on coverage, healthy check-ins, and open detections

goals.title: Segment the network and secure remote access
goals.objective: You will enforce firewall rules, separate networks into trust zones, and require secure authenticated remote access with no direct exposure of internal services.
goals.why: Reduces the blast radius of a breach by limiting lateral movement and removing risky direct paths into the network.
kpis: Percent of external-facing systems behind a segmentation or firewall review (target 100 percent)
Percent of remote access sessions requiring multi-factor authentication (target 100 percent)
Number of unmanaged internal services directly reachable from the internet (target 0)
milestones: Document current network zones and map traffic flows between them
Segment guest, user, server, and management networks with firewall rules between zones
Replace direct remote access with a VPN or zero trust gateway requiring MFA
Review and tighten firewall rules to a default-deny posture with documented exceptions
Enable logging on firewalls and remote access gateways and forward logs for monitoring

goals.title: Build secure development and software supply chain practices
goals.objective: You will scan code and dependencies, track your software components, and test applications for vulnerabilities before and after release.
goals.why: Reduces the risk of shipping exploitable flaws or inheriting compromised third-party and open-source components.
kpis: Percent of code repositories with automated dependency scanning enabled (target 100 percent)
Mean time to remediate critical application vulnerabilities (target under 30 days)
Percent of production applications with a current software bill of materials (target 90 percent+)
milestones: Adopt secure coding standards and add peer review to the development workflow
Enable automated dependency and secrets scanning in the code pipeline
Generate and maintain a software bill of materials for each application
Add static application security testing to the build pipeline with failing gates for critical issues
Schedule periodic dynamic testing or penetration testing of external-facing applications
Define an SLA and triage process for security findings from all testing sources

goals.title: Stand up centralized logging, monitoring, and threat detection
goals.objective: Critical systems will forward logs to a central store where a SIEM runs prioritized detection use cases and alerts a responsible owner.
goals.why: You cannot respond to attacks you never see, and centralized detection shortens the window in which an intruder can act unnoticed.
kpis: Percent of critical systems forwarding logs to the central store (target 100%)
Number of tuned, documented detection use cases in production (target at least 10)
Mean time to detect for validated incidents (target under 24 hours and falling)
Percent of high-severity alerts triaged within the defined SLA (target 95%)
milestones: Inventory critical systems and identify the log sources each must send
Deploy or configure a central log store and enforce a minimum retention period
Onboard endpoints, servers, network devices, and cloud accounts to the SIEM
Build and tune an initial set of prioritized detection use cases with clear owners
Define alert severities, triage steps, and an on-call routing path
Run a monthly review to retire noisy rules and add new detections

goals.title: Build a tested incident response capability
goals.objective: You will have an approved incident response plan with named roles, scenario playbooks, and a practiced tabletop exercise cadence.
goals.why: A rehearsed plan turns a chaotic breach into a coordinated response, reducing damage, downtime, and legal exposure.
kpis: Percent of defined IR roles with a named primary and backup (target 100%)
Number of scenario playbooks published (target at least 4 covering common cases)
Number of tabletop exercises completed per year (target at least 2)
Mean time to respond for validated incidents (target under 72 hours and falling)
milestones: Draft and approve an incident response plan covering detection through recovery
Assign incident roles including lead, communications, and legal or executive contact
Write playbooks for high-likelihood scenarios such as ransomware and account compromise
Establish a reporting path to leadership and required external parties
Run a tabletop exercise and capture lessons learned in an action log
Review and update the plan after each exercise or real incident

goals.title: Establish tested backups, recovery objectives, and continuity
goals.objective: Critical data and systems will have protected backups, defined recovery objectives, and continuity plans that are proven by regular test restores.
goals.why: Reliable, tested recovery is the single strongest defense against ransomware and destructive incidents that would otherwise halt the business.
kpis: Percent of critical systems with a successful test restore in the last quarter (target 100%)
Percent of critical data covered by backups that include an offline or immutable copy (target 100%)
Defined recovery time objective and recovery point objective for each critical system (target documented for 100%)
Gap between actual test-restore time and the recovery time objective (target zero or negative)
milestones: Identify critical systems and data and set a recovery time and recovery point objective for each
Implement backups that follow a resilient pattern with an offline or immutable copy
Document recovery procedures step by step for each critical system
Schedule and perform test restores at least quarterly and log the results
Draft a business continuity plan for extended outages of key services
Review objectives and coverage whenever systems or data change materially

goals.title: Run role-based awareness training and phishing simulations
goals.objective: All staff will complete role-based security training on a set cadence and take part in recurring phishing simulations with tracked results.
goals.why: People are the most targeted layer, and a trained, tested workforce sharply lowers the odds a phishing email or social engineering ploy succeeds.
kpis: Percent of staff who completed required training this period (target 95% or higher)
Phishing simulation click rate (target under 5% and falling)
Phishing report rate, meaning percent of recipients who report the test (target rising above the click rate)
Percent of high-risk roles completing added role-specific training (target 100%)
milestones: Define baseline training for all staff and added modules for high-risk roles
Select or build training content in plain language and set a delivery cadence
Launch a recurring phishing simulation program with escalating difficulty
Track completion and simulation results and follow up with non-responders
Provide short refreshers targeted at repeat clickers
Report awareness metrics and trends to leadership each quarter

goals.title: Manage third-party and supply chain risk
goals.objective: You will maintain a vendor inventory ranked by risk, with security due diligence and security terms in contracts for critical suppliers.
goals.why: A breach or outage at a vendor can flow straight into your business, so knowing and vetting your suppliers closes a major blind spot.
kpis: Percent of vendors captured in the inventory with a data-access and criticality rating (target 100%)
Percent of critical vendors with a completed security review (target 100%)
Percent of critical vendor contracts including security and breach-notification terms (target 100%)
Percent of critical vendors reviewed within the defined cycle, for example annually (target 100%)
milestones: Build a vendor inventory and record what data and access each vendor holds
Rank vendors by criticality and the sensitivity of the data they touch
Define a due diligence process sized to each vendor's risk tier
Complete security reviews for all critical vendors
Add security, breach-notification, and right-to-audit terms to critical contracts
Set a recurring review cycle and an offboarding checklist for ending vendors

goals.title: Drive continuous improvement with metrics, audit, and testing
goals.objective: The program will run on tracked metrics, periodic internal audits, and regular penetration testing that feed a managed remediation backlog.
goals.why: Measuring, auditing, and testing the program turns security from a one-time project into a system that keeps pace with new threats.
kpis: Percent of program metrics reported to leadership on the defined cadence (target 100%)
Number of internal audits or control self-assessments completed per year (target at least 1)
Percent of penetration test findings remediated within their SLA by severity (target 90% or higher)
Mean time to remediate high-severity findings from audits and tests (target within SLA and falling)
milestones: Define a small set of program metrics and a reporting cadence to leadership
Establish an internal audit or control self-assessment schedule against a chosen framework
Commission periodic penetration testing scoped to critical systems
Track all findings in a single prioritized remediation backlog with owners and SLAs
Hold a recurring management review of metrics, findings, and roadmap progress
Feed lessons learned back into policies, controls, and next-cycle goals
